caption:
ANI and The Wire both carried the same piece this April: as influence becomes boardroom currency, executive presence is emerging as a strategic imperative. Fast Company made the case in October. boardsi made it again in February. Three separate desks, one conclusion.

This matters because the objection to presence work has always been the same "soft skills, nice to have, not a line item." The business press has now filed it under strategy, not personality.

Which means you no longer have to argue for it on your own behalf. The argument is on the record.

Presence is not charisma. It is bearing, tone, and the discipline to hold a silence while the room decides. In command, those were trainable. Measurable. Assessed. They still are.

If your ideas only land when someone else repeats them, the gap is not competence. It is command signal and that can be built.

topic.title: Executive presence named a boardroom strategic imperative
topic.angle: Lumina's hardest objection is that executive presence sounds like soft-skills fluff, and Indian business-press framing it as a board-level strategic variable gives managers and owners the third-party justification self-promotion can't supply.
